images.title: Square lockers stay open
images.purpose: Shows all 100 lockers in a 10 by 10 grid: the 10 square numbered lockers stand open and every other locker is closed.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large 10 by 10 grid of small locker doors in the centre, with one short tag below it.
images.exact_structure: Exactly 100 small equal locker doors in a 10 by 10 grid, numbered in reading order 1 to 100 from the top left, row by row, but with no numbers drawn on the doors except the corner tags. Exactly 10 doors are drawn swung open and filled reddish purple (#CC79A7): row 1 columns 1, 4 and 9; row 2 column 6; row 3 column 5; row 4 column 6; row 5 column 9; row 7 column 4; row 9 column 1; row 10 column 10 (lockers 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 81, 100). The other 90 doors are closed, white with a thin grey (#6B7280) outline. A small tag 1 sits above the top left door and a small tag 100 below the bottom right door. Under the grid, one short tag: a reddish purple (#CC79A7) swatch with open: 10 squares. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The lockers left open are exactly the square numbers.
images.description: Shows all 100 lockers in a 10 by 10 grid: the 10 square numbered lockers stand open and every other locker is closed.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the open lockers scattered over the full grid makes the square number answer concrete.
